pages.ko: 옛날 옛날 아주 먼 옛날에, 파도 소리가 늘 들리는 바닷가 마을에 마음씨 착한 총각 덕이가 살았어요. 덕이는 가진 것이 하나도 없어 배가 꼬르륵거리는 날이 많았지요. 그래도 나무 한 짐을 팔면 반은 이웃집 담 너머로 슬쩍 놓고 왔답니다. "나눠 먹으면 더 맛있잖아요!"
pages.t: Long, long ago, in a village by the sea where you could always hear the waves, there lived a kind young man named Deok-i. He owned nothing at all, and many a day his tummy went rumble-rumble. Still, whenever he sold a load of firewood, he would quietly leave half of it over his neighbor's wall. "Everything tastes better when you share it!"

pages.ko: 어느 추운 겨울날, 덕이가 산에 나무를 하러 갔어요. 그런데 눈길 바위 옆에 흰 수염 할아버지가 오들오들 떨고 앉아 있지 뭐예요. 덕이는 품에 품고 있던 주먹밥 한 덩이를 통째로 내밀었어요. "할아버지, 이거 드세요. 저는 이따 먹으면 돼요."
pages.t: One cold winter day, Deok-i went up the mountain to gather firewood. And there, beside a snowy rock, sat a white-bearded old man, shivering and shaking! Deok-i pulled out the one rice ball he had been keeping warm inside his coat and held it out. "Grandfather, please eat this. I can eat later."

pages.ko: 할아버지는 빙그레 웃으며 작고 동그란 맷돌 하나를 꺼냈어요. "갖고 싶은 것을 부르며 돌려 보렴." 드르륵— "쌀 나와라, 뚝딱! 쌀 나와라, 뚝딱!" 정말로 하얀 쌀이 솨아 쏟아졌어요! "멈출 때는 그만 뚝딱, 그만 뚝딱! 이 말을 꼭 기억하렴."
pages.t: The old man smiled a warm smile and took out a small, round millstone. "Turn it, and call out whatever you wish for." Rrrumble— "Rice, come out, pop pop! Rice, come out, pop pop!" And truly, white rice came pouring out — whoosh! "And to stop it, say: Stop now, pop pop! Stop now, pop pop! Be sure you remember those words."

pages.ko: 집에 돌아온 덕이는 맷돌을 방바닥에 놓고 조심조심 돌렸어요. "쌀 나와라, 뚝딱!" 솨아— 쌀이 소복소복! "이불 나와라, 뚝딱!" 폭신한 이불이 톡! 덕이는 얼른 "그만 뚝딱, 그만 뚝딱!" 하고 멈추었어요. 꼭 쓸 만큼만 말이에요.
pages.t: Back home, Deok-i set the millstone on the floor and turned it ever so carefully. "Rice, come out, pop pop!" Whoosh — the rice piled up soft and high! "Blanket, come out, pop pop!" And plop! — out came a fluffy blanket. Then Deok-i quickly said, "Stop now, pop pop! Stop now, pop pop!" Just enough, and not one bit more.

pages.ko: 이튿날 덕이는 마당으로 이웃들을 다 불렀어요. "콩 나와라, 뚝딱! 팥 나와라, 뚝딱!" 덕이는 됫박으로 곡식을 되어 집집마다 나누어 주고, 시루에 김이 모락모락 나는 떡을 쪄서 함께 먹었지요. "그만 뚝딱, 그만 뚝딱!" 맷돌은 언제나 알맞은 데서 멈췄답니다.
pages.t: The next day Deok-i called all his neighbors into his yard. "Beans, come out, pop pop! Red beans, come out, pop pop!" He measured out the grain with his wooden measuring box and shared some with every house, and he steamed rice cakes in a big earthenware steamer until they puffed clouds of warm steam, and everyone ate together. "Stop now, pop pop! Stop now, pop pop!" The millstone always stopped at just the right moment.

pages.ko: 잔치가 파할 무렵, 담 너머로 뒤늦게 기웃거리던 욕심쟁이 도둑이 눈을 반짝였어요. '나와라 뚝딱' 하면 무엇이든 나온다지? 딱 그 말만 듣고 도둑은 히죽 웃었지요. "저 맷돌만 있으면 나는 세상에서 제일가는 부자다!" 깜깜한 밤, 도둑은 살금살금 방으로 들어와 맷돌을 궤에 쏙 넣고 등에 짊어졌어요. 그러고는 바닷가 쪽으로 뚜벅뚜벅 달아났지요.
pages.t: As the feast was ending, a greedy thief who had come too late stood peeking over the wall, and his eyes lit up. So anything at all comes out if you say "come out, pop pop"? That was every word he heard, and he grinned a sly grin. "With that millstone, I'll be the richest man in the whole world!" In the pitch-dark night, the thief crept into the room, tucked the millstone into a wooden chest, and hoisted it onto his back. Then off he ran, thump, thump, thump, down toward the sea.

pages.ko: 바닷가에 매어 둔 작은 배에 도둑은 빈 소금가마니를 잔뜩 실었어요. "소금은 값이 비싸지! 배가 넘치도록 갈아서 몽땅 팔아야지." 도둑은 노를 힘껏 저어 먼바다로 나아갔어요. 마을은 점점 작아져서 콩알만 해졌답니다.
pages.t: At the shore he loaded a little boat with piles of empty salt sacks. "Salt sells for a lot of money! I'll grind till the boat is overflowing, then sell every last bit of it." The thief pulled hard on his oar and headed far out to sea. The village grew smaller and smaller, until it was no bigger than a bean.

pages.ko: 바다 한가운데서 도둑은 맷돌을 무릎 앞에 놓고 드르륵 돌렸어요. "소금 나와라, 뚝딱! 소금 나와라, 뚝딱!" 하얀 소금이 솨아— 쏟아지기 시작했어요. "히히, 부자다 부자!" 도둑은 갑판 위에서 덩실덩실 춤을 추었지요.
pages.t: Out in the middle of the sea, the thief set the millstone down in front of his knees and turned it — rrrumble. "Salt, come out, pop pop! Salt, come out, pop pop!" White salt began to pour out — whoosh! "Hee hee, I'm rich, I'm rich!" And the thief danced a wobbly little dance right there on the deck.

pages.ko: 그런데 소금은 멈추지 않았어요. 솨아, 솨아, 솨아— 가마니가 툭툭 터지고, 갑판이 하얗게 덮이고, 소금은 자꾸자꾸 쌓여 커다란 산이 되었어요. 배가 기우뚱, 기우뚱!
pages.t: But the salt did not stop. Whoosh, whoosh, whoosh — the sacks burst open, the deck turned white all over, and the salt piled higher and higher into a great big mountain. The boat tipped this way, and tipped that way!

pages.ko: "그, 그만! 멈춰! 서라! 섰거라!" 도둑은 목이 터져라 소리쳤지만 맷돌은 들은 척도 하지 않았어요. 멈추는 말을 배우지도 않고 훔쳐 왔으니까요. "그만… 그만 뭐였더라!" 도둑의 얼굴이 소금보다 더 하얘졌답니다.
pages.t: "S-stop! Stop it! Halt! Whoa there!" The thief shouted till his throat was sore, but the millstone paid him no mind at all. He had stolen it without ever learning the words that make it stop. "Stop now… stop now, what was it again?" The thief's face went whiter than the salt.

pages.ko: 쿠르릉— 배가 기우뚱 넘어가고, 맷돌은 소금과 함께 바닷속으로 쏘옥 내려갔어요. 도둑은 첨벙! 물에 빠졌다가 허우적허우적 헤엄쳐 나와, 둥둥 떠 있는 널빤지 하나를 두 팔로 꼭 끌어안았지요. "사, 살려 주세요! 짜다, 짜!"
pages.t: Groooan— the boat tipped right over, and down went the millstone with all the salt, deep into the sea. Splash! The thief fell into the water, paddled and flailed his way back up, and hugged a floating plank tight with both arms. "H-help me! Oh, it's salty, so salty!"

pages.ko: 마침 지나던 고깃배가 도둑을 번쩍 건져 올렸어요. 짠물을 잔뜩 마신 도둑은 콜록콜록, 소금에 절인 무처럼 축 늘어졌지요. "다시는… 다시는 남의 것을 탐내지 않을게요." 마을로 돌아온 도둑은 덕이에게 꾸벅 절을 하고, 그날부터 이웃 일을 도우며 살았답니다.
pages.t: Just then a fishing boat came by and scooped the thief right out of the water. He had swallowed so much salty water that he coughed and coughed, drooping like a radish left too long in the salt. "Never again… never again will I want what belongs to somebody else." Back in the village, the thief bowed low to Deok-i, and from that day on he lived helping his neighbors.

pages.ko: 그럼 바닷속으로 내려간 맷돌은 어떻게 되었을까요? 아무도 "그만 뚝딱!" 하고 말해 주지 않아서, 맷돌은 지금도 드르륵드르륵 소금을 갈고 있대요. 그래서 바닷물이 이렇게 짜답니다. 덕이는 여전히 됫박으로 곡식을 되어 이웃과 나누며 살았지요. 알맞은 데서 멈출 줄 아는 마음, 그게 진짜 보물이래요.
pages.t: So what happened to the millstone that went down into the sea? Nobody ever said "Stop now, pop pop!" to it — so it is still down there grinding salt, rrrumble, rrrumble, even today. And that is why the sea is so very salty. As for Deok-i, he went on measuring out grain in his wooden box and sharing it with his neighbors. Knowing how to stop at just the right moment — they say that is the real treasure.
